why: The answer correctly names String as the type that isn't primitive and gives one reason (it is a class), but it never applies the idea to the code's lines or values or relates it to anything else.

concepts.why: It correctly sorts int, double, boolean and char as primitive types, but only names them.
It correctly says String is a non-primitive class type, but only names it.
It never says that a primitive variable holds its value while a reference variable holds an address.
It says nothing about data types as sets of values and operations.
